records.question: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
search_queries: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
records.answer:
Graduate students on F-1 or J-1 status need to register for **at least 9 credits each term** to be full-time.

Some conditions to keep in mind:
- **Online courses:** Only 3 credits of online or distance coursework can count toward full-time enrollment each term. That means at least 6 of your credits must be face-to-face or hybrid.
- **Audited courses:** These don't count toward the full-time minimum.
- **Less than full time (LTFT):** If you can't register full-time, you need written permission from ISSS *before* the term begins or before you drop below full-time. LTFT requests need your academic advisor's approval and must be submitted by the add/drop deadline, or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7).
- **Dropping or withdrawing:** Don't drop or withdraw from a course during the semester without first getting approval from an ISSS advisor.

Students who don't enroll full-time and don't get LTFT authorization are considered out of immigration status. For questions about your own situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How many online credits can count toward my full-time enrollment each term?
search_queries: How many online credits can count toward my full-time enrollment each term?
records.answer:
**No more than 3 credits of online or distance coursework can count toward your full-time enrollment each term.**

What that means in practice:
- Undergraduates (12+ credits required) need at least 9 credits that are face-to-face or hybrid.
- Graduate students (9+ credits required) need at least 6 credits that are face-to-face or hybrid.
- Hybrid classes count as in-person for immigration purposes, per a 2023 ISSS announcement.
- Audited courses don't count toward the full-time minimum.
- In your final term, you can't take courses fully online. If you need more than one class to finish, you can count no more than one class (3 credits) of online study.

Don't drop or withdraw from a course mid-semester without first getting approval from an ISSS advisor. If you want to enroll in fewer than full-time credits, you need written ISSS permission before you drop below full-time.

Older announcements (from 2020 and 2023) describe temporary COVID-era flexibilities. Those flexibilities have ended, and the 3-credit limit is the current rule on the ISSS pages.

For questions about your own situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor (isss@drexel.edu).

records.question: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?
search_queries: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?
records.answer:
**Up to 20 hours per week** while school is in session. During an approved vacation term, F-1 and J-1 students may work more than 20 hours per week, but you should check the Office of Human Resources for their policies on working on campus during that time.

Key conditions:
- You must be maintaining valid F-1/J-1 status, be a continuing student who hasn't graduated, and have an unexpired I-20/DS-2019.
- J-1 students must receive prior ISSS authorization for any on-campus employment.
- If you're on co-op, your co-op counts as your "class," so on-campus work is still limited to 20 hours per week. ISSS strongly discourages doing both at the same time.
- Work must not hurt your academic performance. Failing or dropping classes can affect your full-time enrollment and may lead to termination of your SEVIS record.

records.question: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
search_queries: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
records.answer:
F-1 students have a **60-day grace period** after their program ends. The same 60 days applies after Post-Completion OPT ends, but only if you completed the OPT. Students who exceeded the 90-day unemployment limit aren't eligible for it.

**During the grace period you may:**
- Prepare to leave the U.S.
- Travel within the U.S.

You may **not** work or study. If you aren't applying for OPT or extending your legal status, you're expected to leave the U.S. during this time. If you leave before it ends, you can't re-enter on your F-1 status after your I-20 expiration date.

**Other options:** You can also use the period to transfer your SEVIS record or start a new program at Drexel or another SEVP-certified school, or to change your immigration status. If USCIS receives your OPT application before the 60 days end, your F-1 status stays active until you get a decision.

**Possible future change:** A 2025 ISSS announcement said DHS had proposed shortening the F-1 grace period to 30 days. That was a proposal, and the ISSS pages I found still list 60 days. The recent announcements list shows a final rule on Duration of Status was published in July 2026 and that a court postponed its effective date in September 2026. I don't have the details of either, so please confirm with an ISSS advisor how this affects your situation.

records.question: How much OPT can I get?
search_queries: How much OPT can I get?
records.answer:
**Standard OPT:** F-1 students get a total of 12 months of OPT per degree level (Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate). You can use some of it during your program (Pre-Completion OPT) or save all 12 months for after graduation (Post-Completion OPT).

- Pre-completion full-time OPT counts at 100% (6 months used = 6 months deducted).
- Pre-completion part-time OPT counts at 50% (6 months used = 3 months deducted).

**STEM OPT Extension:** If you're in a STEM field and meet the criteria, you may be eligible for an additional 24 months of Post-Completion OPT. You can't request all 36 months (12+24) at once. You must first apply for the initial 12 months of Post-Completion OPT, then apply for the STEM extension while your OPT EAD card is still active.

**Proposed rule:** On October 9, 2026, ISSS announced that DHS has proposed a $70,000 fee for OPT and a $30,000 fee for STEM OPT, to be paid by universities. ISSS says this has no immediate impact: current OPT and STEM OPT processes are unchanged unless DHS finalizes and implements the rule after the public comment period.

For your specific situation, contact ISSS at isss@drexel.edu.

records.question: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
search_queries: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
records.answer:
You can be unemployed for a maximum of **90 days** in total (an aggregate limit) while on Post-Completion OPT.

- **How days are counted:** Every day, including weekends, between the start of your OPT authorization (the employment start date on your EAD) and the end that you don't have qualifying employment counts as a day of unemployment.
- **Working hours:** Post-Completion OPT work must be at least 20 hours per week. If you're worried about meeting that, contact ISSS.
- **If you reach the limit:** Exceeding 90 days is a violation of F-1 status, and your SEVIS record may be terminated. Before you reach the limit, you should prepare to transfer schools, change educational level, depart the U.S., or otherwise maintain status. Students who exceed 90 days are not eligible for the 60-day grace period.
- **STEM OPT:** If you're later approved for the 24-month STEM extension, you get an additional 60 unemployment days, for a maximum of 150 days total. You must report any interruption or loss of employment to ISSS.

For your own situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
search_queries: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
records.answer:
**No, a job offer is not required to apply for OPT.** The ISSS OPT page states this directly.

Some conditions apply once you're on OPT:

- **Post-Completion OPT:** You're expected to actively look for work in your field and be employed for at least nine months after your OPT start date (as shown on your EAD). F-1 status depends on employment during this period, and you can accrue an aggregate maximum of 90 days of unemployment. Before you reach that limit, you should prepare to transfer schools, change educational level, depart the U.S., or otherwise maintain status.
- **Pre-Completion OPT:** There is no penalty for not working, but any time you don't work still counts against your 12 months of OPT eligibility.
- **STEM OPT extension:** This is different. You need a job or job offer directly related to your STEM degree, from an employer that participates in E-Verify.

You also can't start working until you have your EAD card and the start date on it has arrived. USCIS can take 90 days or longer to process applications.

For advice on your own situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
search_queries: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
records.answer:
No. According to the ISSS STEM OPT page, self-employment is not eligible for a STEM OPT extension. The regulations require a bona fide employer-employee relationship with an employer, and you may not provide employer attestations on your own behalf.

A few related points from ISSS:
- You can work for a start-up business, but all regulatory requirements must still be met, and you cannot attest on your own behalf as the employer.
- Your STEM OPT employer must have an EIN, be enrolled in and using E-Verify at your worksite, and the job must be directly related to your STEM degree.
- Unpaid or volunteer positions also can't be the basis for a STEM OPT extension.

This differs from the standard 12-month Post-Completion OPT, where ISSS says you may be a self-employed business owner if you work full-time, hold the proper business licenses, and are actively engaged in a business related to your degree.

If you're planning a business or start-up and want to apply for STEM OPT, I recommend confirming your specific situation with an ISSS advisor before you apply.

records.question: Does my employer need to use E-Verify for my STEM OPT?
search_queries: Does my employer need to use E-Verify for my STEM OPT?
records.answer:
Yes. Your STEM OPT employer must be enrolled in E-Verify and using it at your STEM OPT worksite. ISSS states that if an employer is not enrolled in E-Verify, a STEM student cannot obtain the 24-month OPT extension.

**What to do:**
- Ask your supervisor or the company's HR department for the employer's E-Verify number. You'll need to list it on the STEM OPT Request Form, and on the Employment Update Form if you report a new employer or an employer change.
- The employer must also meet the other STEM OPT requirements: it needs an EIN, the job must be directly related to your qualifying STEM degree, and there must be an employer-employee relationship (self-employment and staffing or temporary agencies likely won't qualify).
- The employer must complete and sign the I-983 training plan.

If your employer isn't sure whether it's enrolled, or you have questions about your own situation, I'd recommend confirming with an ISSS advisor (ISSS@drexel.edu, 215.895.2502).

Please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

**How to request one:** A December 2024 [re-entry advisory](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2024/December/re-entry) links the Signature Request form: [Signature Request form](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs). records.question: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?

records.question: What happens if I'm away from Drexel and not enrolled for more than five months?
search_queries: What happens if I'm away from Drexel and not enrolled for more than five months?
records.answer:
If you are not enrolled for more than five months, you will need a new I-20/DS-2019 to return to the U.S. A SEVIS reactivation is only an option for authorized absences of less than five months.

**What it involves:**
- You must apply for and receive a new I-20/DS-2019 and repay the SEVIS I-901 fee. The same applies if your SEVIS record was terminated for reasons other than "Authorized Early Withdrawal."
- Email ISSS at least three (3) months before your planned return to get instructions on applying for the new I-20/DS-2019.
- Because this kind of absence creates a break in your F-1 status, you must complete at least one academic year of full-time study after you return before you become eligible for certain F-1 benefits, such as CPT or OPT.
- You also need approval from your academic program to return from a leave of absence. Contact your academic advisor for instructions on reporting your return to Drexel.

For comparison, if your absence was authorized by ISSS and lasts less than five months, you can request a SEVIS reactivation. That process is subject to SEVP discretion. If SEVP does not approve it, you would need a new I-20 instead.

Since this affects your immigration status, please confirm your specific situation with an ISSS advisor before you leave or plan your return. Also connect with ISSS before taking a leave of absence.

records.question: Can I take less than a full course load in my final term?
search_queries: Can I take less than a full course load in my final term?
records.answer:
Yes, you may be able to. F-1 and J-1 students in the final term of their degree program can apply for less than full-time (LTFT) enrollment if the credits they still need to finish their program are fewer than what full-time enrollment requires.

**Key conditions**
- You can't take courses fully online in your final term. If you need more than one class to finish, you can count no more than one class (3 credits) of online study toward your remaining requirements.
- You must get ISSS authorization *before* you drop below full-time. Students who go below full-time without approval are considered out of status.
- Full-time is 12+ credits for undergraduates and 9+ for graduate students.

**How to apply**
1. Complete the Less Than Full-Time form on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx?source=https%3a%2f%2fdrexel0.sharepoint.com%2fsites%2fISSS-StudentPortal%2fSitePages%2fForms%2fByAuthor.aspx).
2. Have your academic advisor specify the reason and sign it.
3. Email it to isss@drexel.edu before you drop below full-time, by the add/drop deadline or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7).
4. Wait for ISSS's email approving or rejecting the request.

Also, don't drop or withdraw from a course mid-term without first getting approval from an ISSS advisor.

If you have a specific situation, such as how many credits you have left, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How do I apply for a reduced course load for medical reasons?
search_queries: How do I apply for a reduced course load for medical reasons?
records.answer:
To apply for a medical reduced course load (LTFT), you need ISSS approval **before** you drop below full-time.

**Steps**
1. **Get a medical letter.** It must be on official letterhead, signed by a licensed medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, or licensed clinical psychologist. It should say that, in their medical opinion, you can't attend classes (or can't attend full-time) during a specific term. The doctor should use the ISSS template letter, which includes your name and date of birth and the term and year. The doctor doesn't have to give diagnosis details. If you can't take any courses, the letter must say so clearly.
2. **Complete the Less Than Full-Time form** on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx?source=https%3a%2f%2fdrexel0.sharepoint.com%2fsites%2fISSS-StudentPortal%2fSitePages%2fForms%2fByAuthor.aspx). Your academic advisor must state the reason and sign it.
3. **Email the form and the doctor's letter together as one PDF** to isss@drexel.edu.
4. **Wait for ISSS's decision by email** before dropping any courses.

**Key conditions**
- Submit by the add/drop deadline, or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7 of the term).
- Approval is needed for each term you request.
- Medical LTFT is limited to 12 aggregate months per program level.
- You're expected to return to full-time study afterward.
- If you're in your final term, you must still enroll in at least one course under medical LTFT.

Dropping below full-time without authorization puts you out of immigration status.

records.question: How do I apply for the STEM OPT extension?
search_queries: How do I apply for the STEM OPT extension?
records.answer:
To apply for the STEM OPT extension, you first request a STEM OPT I-20 from ISSS, then file your I-765 with USCIS online.

**Timing**
- You can file up to 90 days before your Post-Completion OPT end date.
- USCIS must receive your application before your OPT EAD card expires. Otherwise you won't be eligible for the extension.
- Send your documents to ISSS at least 30 days before your EAD end date.
- USCIS must receive your application within 60 days of the date ISSS prints your STEM OPT I-20.

**Steps**
1. **Complete Form I-983.** Download it from [DHS Study in the States](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/stem-opt-hub/additional-resources/form-i-983-overview) (external). You submit it to ISSS, not USCIS.
2. **Email isss@drexel.edu** to request the STEM OPT I-20. Attach, as individual PDFs or one compiled PDF (no zip files):
   - STEM OPT Request Form
   - Completed I-983
   - STEM OPT processing fee receipt
   - Scan of your current OPT EAD card (front and back)
   - Passport scan (valid at least 6 months)
   - Most recent I-94
   - Official transcript for your STEM degree
   - If you are applying based on a previous STEM degree: the I-20 from that degree and its official transcript
3. **File the I-765 online with USCIS.** ISSS emails you the I-20 and the filing instructions once it has reviewed your request.

If your EAD expires while a timely application is pending, you may keep working up to 180 days with your I-797 receipt notice.

Full details are on the [STEM OPT Extension page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension). For questions about your own situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: What documents do I need to re-enter the U.S. after a trip abroad as an F-1 student?

records.question: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
search_queries: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
records.answer:
**CPT and OPT are both F-1 off-campus work authorizations, but they work differently.**

**CPT (Curricular Practical Training)**
- It applies only when an internship, co-op, practicum, or similar training is a required part of your specific academic program.
- It is driven by the curriculum, not by your wish to work. Employment that is only beneficial or relevant doesn't qualify.
- ISSS reviews and authorizes it.
- Dates follow the official term dates in the Drexel academic calendar. Authorization is term by term, except for Steinbright co-op programs, which follow the co-op cycle dates.

**OPT (Optional Practical Training)**
- It lets you work in temporary employment directly related to your major and appropriate to your degree level.
- It is available before you complete your studies (Pre-Completion) and after (Post-Completion).
- You can use it even if CPT isn't an option. A job offer isn't required to apply.
- USCIS decides on OPT applications, not ISSS, and it can take 90 days or longer.
- Eligibility requires at least one full academic year of full-time enrollment in the U.S., lawful F-1 status, and fewer than 365 days of full-time CPT at your current level.

**How they connect:** Using 364 days or more of full-time CPT eliminates your OPT eligibility. Part-time CPT or international co-op does not affect it.

For advice on your own situation, check with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: I graduated and my OPT is approved. What do I need to travel abroad and come back?

records.question: Will doing CPT affect my OPT eligibility?
search_queries: Will doing CPT affect my OPT eligibility?
records.answer:
Yes, it can, depending on the type of CPT you use.

- **Full-time CPT for one year (364 days) or more eliminates your eligibility for OPT.** The OPT page says you need fewer than 365 days of full-time CPT at your current educational level. Accumulating more than 364 days is also listed as a common reason OPT applications are denied.

records.question: Can I work an on-campus job while I'm on co-op?
search_queries: Can I work an on-campus job while I'm on co-op?
records.answer:
Yes, but ISSS strongly discourages it. F-1 and J-1 students may work on campus while on co-op, with these conditions:

- **20-hour limit:** During your co-op cycle, your co-op job counts as your "class," so on-campus work is limited to 20 hours per week.
- **No impact on the co-op:** On-campus work must not interfere with your responsibilities at your co-op job.
- **Valid status:** You must be maintaining valid F-1/J-1 status, your I-20/DS-2019 must not have expired, and you must not have graduated.
- **J-1 students:** You must get ISSS permission before starting any on-campus job. Email isss@drexel.edu with a copy of your job offer, including the position title and expected start and end dates, before accepting it.
- **F-1 students:** You don't need advance ISSS approval, but you do need to complete onboarding and the I-9 with Drexel HR.

Drexel HR may have its own (non-immigration) policies about working on campus during this time, so check with them too.

If you're unsure whether your situation fits these rules, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Tôi có thể làm CPT trong năm học đầu tiên không?

**Thông thường là không.** Theo trang CPT của ISSS, bạn phải đã học toàn thời gian trong chương trình cấp bằng và có mặt tại Mỹ ít nhất một năm học đầy đủ (3 quý hoặc 2 học kỳ) trước khi đủ điều kiện làm CPT.

**Các điều kiện khác của CPT:**
- Bạn phải có lời mời thực tập/đào tạo liên quan trực tiếp đến ngành học.

- Nếu có môn học đi kèm, bạn phải đăng ký môn đó trong kỳ được cấp CPT.
- CPT thường giới hạn 20 giờ/tuần (có một số ngoại lệ, ví dụ co-op toàn thời gian).

records.question: OPT申请需要多长时间？
search_queries: OPT申请需要多长时间？
records.answer:
**OPT申请的处理时间：** USCIS审理OPT申请可能需要**90天或更长时间**。最新的处理时间可以在[USCIS案件处理时间页面](https://egov.uscis.gov/processing-times)查看（外部链接）。

**整个流程中的其他时间点：**
- **ISSS签发OPT I-20：** 收到您完整的申请后，大约需要4-5个工作日。
- **向USCIS提交I-765：** 必须在OPT I-20（OPT推荐）签发后30天内提交。
- **申请时间窗口：**
  - 毕业前OPT（Pre-Completion）：最早可在希望开始日期前90天申请。
  - 毕业后OPT（Post-Completion）：最早可在项目结束日前90天申请，最晚为完成学位要求后60天内。
- **收据通知：** USCIS收到申请后约2-3周会邮寄OPT Receipt Notice给您。

**建议：** 因为审理时间可能超过90天，可以考虑选择比实际入职日期更早的OPT开始日期，并尽早申请。在拿到EAD（工作许可卡）之前不能开始工作。

**加急处理：** ISSS的一则2023年公告提到，USCIS曾推出I-907加急处理（费用$1,500，30个日历日）。这是较早的公告，费用和资格可能已变化，请向ISSS顾问确认目前是否适用。

records.question: ¿Cuántas horas por semana puedo trabajar en el campus?

- Los estudiantes J-1 necesitan autorización previa de ISSS para cualquier empleo en el campus.
- Excepción: si tu currículo te exige trabajar más de 20 horas por semana en el campus, debes solicitar CPT.

records.question: 졸업 후 F-1 학생의 유예 기간은 얼마나 되나요?
search_queries: 졸업 후 F-1 학생의 유예 기간은 얼마나 되나요?
records.answer:
F-1 학생의 졸업(프로그램 종료) 후 유예 기간은 **60일**입니다. (J-1 학생은 30일입니다.)

**유예 기간 중 할 수 있는 것:**
- 짐을 정리하고 미국을 떠날 준비를 하는 것
- 미국 내 여행

**유예 기간 중 할 수 없는 것:** 근무 및 수학

유예 기간 동안 OPT를 신청하거나 체류 자격 연장을 받지 않는 학생은 출국해야 합니다. 유예 기간이 끝나기 전에 출국하면, I-20 만료일 이후에는 F-1 신분으로 재입국할 수 없습니다.

**OPT 관련:** OPT 또는 STEM OPT가 끝난 후(EAD 카드 만료 후)에도 60일의 유예 기간이 있습니다. 다만 OPT 기간 중 허용된 실업 일수(OPT 90일, STEM OPT 150일)를 초과한 학생은 유예 기간을 받을 수 없습니다.

**앞으로의 변경 가능성:** 2025년 9월에 DHS가 유예 기간을 30일로 줄이는 내용을 포함한 규정을 제안했습니다. 이후 2026년 7월 17일에 DHS가 체류 기간(D/S)을 폐지하는 최종 규정을 발표했으나, 2026년 9월 14일 연방 지방법원이 그 시행을 연기하는 예비 금지명령을 내렸습니다. 제가 확인한 자료에는 이 최종 규정의 유예 기간 세부 내용이 나와 있지 않으므로, 본인의 상황에 적용되는 내용은 ISSS 어드바이저에게 확인하시기 바랍니다.

records.question: Do I pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again after a long leave?
search_queries: Do I pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again after a long leave?
records.answer:
It depends on how long you're away and why.

**You must repay the SEVIS I-901 fee if:**
- You have not been enrolled for more than five (5) months, or
- Your SEVIS record was terminated for reasons other than "Authorized Early Withdrawal."

In those cases you need a new I-20/DS-2019. Email ISSS at least three (3) months before your planned return for instructions. Because this creates a break in F-1 status, you must complete at least one academic year of full-time study after returning before you become eligible for certain F-1 benefits, such as CPT or OPT.

**You don't need a new I-20 (and the page doesn't mention a new fee) if:**
- ISSS authorized your absence and your break is under five (5) months. You can request a SEVIS reactivation by submitting these at least 1-2 months before returning:
  - I-94 travel history showing your departure
  - Flight itinerary showing your planned re-entry date
  - Proof of full-time enrollment for the upcoming term

Reactivation is subject to SEVP discretion. If SEVP denies it, you'll need a new I-20 instead.

Before any of this, you need approval from your academic program to return, so contact your academic advisor.

For your specific situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor (contact details are on the [ISSS website](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support)).

records.question: 212(e) two-year home country requirement
search_queries: 212(e) two-year home country requirement
records.answer:
**What it is:** The two-year home-country physical presence requirement (212(e)) applies to certain J-1 exchange visitors. Until it is met, they can't get lawful permanent residency or change to another visa status in the U.S. They must live and be physically present in their country of nationality or last legal permanent residence for a total of at least two years after leaving the U.S. in J-1 status.

**Who it applies to:**
- Those whose program was financed, in whole or part, directly or indirectly, by the U.S. government or by the government of their country of nationality or last legal residence.
- Those who were a national or resident of a country that the U.S. Department of State has designated as needing people with the specialized knowledge or skill in their field (the "skills list").

For students, ISSS says that government funding or a major on the home country's skills list can make you subject to it.

**H-1B impact:** If you hold or previously held J-1/J-2 status and are subject to 212(e), you can't begin H-1B employment until you receive a waiver of 212(e).

**Waivers:** You may be able to apply for a waiver under certain conditions, but ISSS may not assist with J-1 waivers because the Department of State views it as a conflict of interest. ISSS refers you to the [Department of State (external)](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/study/exchange/waiver-of-the-exchange-visitor.html). Processing can take a year or longer, and applying doesn't extend your legal stay. After a favorable recommendation, you lose eligibility for J-1 extension, transfer, and a new J-1 visa.

To find out whether it applies to you, check with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: H-1B cap-gap extension
search_queries: H-1B cap-gap extension
records.answer:
**H-1B cap-gap in brief:** It covers the period between the end of your OPT (or STEM OPT) and the start of H-1B status. If your employer filed a timely change-of-status petition with an October 1 start date, your work authorization is automatically extended while the petition is pending, until October 1 or until it is approved.

**You're eligible if:**
- Your employer files the H-1B petition on or after April 1 and requests a change of status to H-1B beginning October 1.
- You are still within your OPT/STEM OPT authorization period when the petition is submitted.

**To get a cap-gap I-20:**
1. Email ISSS to confirm your employment and address information is accurate in SEVIS. Missing or wrong information will significantly delay the I-20.
2. Email ISSS one of the following:
   - For a cap-gap through June 1: an employer statement that the change-of-status petition was properly filed, plus proof of delivery to USCIS.
   - For a cap-gap beyond June 1: a scanned USCIS receipt, or proof the petition was wait-listed.

ISSS will email you when the new I-20 is ready.

**Good to know:**
- If the petition is denied, rejected, or revoked and your EAD is still valid, work permission ends on the EAD end date. If your OPT already expired, it ends on the rejection, denial, revocation, or withdrawal date.
- The unemployment limit continues during cap-gap.
- For travel during cap-gap, ISSS suggests checking with your employer and/or immigration attorney.

**Possible change in the end date:** A January 2025 ISSS announcement says the H-1B Modernization Rule extends the cap-gap period from October 1 to as late as April 1 of the following year. The OPT and STEM OPT pages still describe October 1, so please confirm with an ISSS advisor which end date applies to you.

What you need to do depends on how long you're away and whether ISSS authorized the absence.

**1. Get approval from your academic program**
If you take a leave of absence, you must first get approval from your academic program to return. Contact your academic advisor for instructions on reporting your return to Drexel.

**2. Get a valid I-20 (F-1) or DS-2019 (J-1) for re-entry**
- **Authorized absence of less than 5 months:** You can request to reactivate your SEVIS record. Submit these at least 1-2 months before your return:
  - I-94 Travel History as proof of your departure
  - Flight itinerary showing your planned re-entry date
  - Proof of full-time enrollment for the upcoming term (registration records or a letter from your academic advisor)

  SEVP decides whether to approve this. If it doesn't, you'll need a new I-20.
- **More than 5 months not enrolled, or SEVIS terminated for a reason other than "Authorized Early Withdrawal":** You need a new I-20/DS-2019 and must repay the SEVIS I-901 fee. Email ISSS at least 3 months before your planned return. This creates a break in F-1 status, so you must complete at least one academic year of full-time study before becoming eligible for benefits like CPT or OPT.

**3. Prepare your travel documents**
- A valid passport, a valid visa, a recent travel signature on your I-20/DS-2019, and proof of enrollment. The [Signature Request form](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs) is for travel signatures.
- If you need a new visa, ISSS also suggests a Drexel enrollment verification and up-to-date financial documents.

records.answer:
Eligibility for Academic Training (AT) through Drexel requires that you meet all of these:

- Your DS-2019 was issued by Drexel, not an outside agency (such as Fulbright).
- You are primarily in the U.S. to study, rather than to do AT.
- You are in good academic standing.
- The AT is directly related to the major field of study listed on your DS-2019.
- The AT is approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date.
- The AT starts no later than 30 days after your program ends.

Time limits also apply. Bachelor's and master's students get up to 18 months, PhD students up to 36 months, and non-degree students can't extend their DS-2019 beyond 24 months in total. In each case the limit is the length of your degree program if that is shorter, except for non-degree students.

**Note on possible rule changes:** Drexel's ISSS pages mention a DHS final rule on duration of status, and the CPT page says it was scheduled to take effect September 15, 2026. A newer ISSS announcement (September 14, 2026) says a US District Court postponed that effective date. The excerpts I have don't spell out how this affects J-1 Academic Training, so please confirm with an ISSS advisor before making plans. (The 2025 proposed rule mentioned that post-graduation AT might require a USCIS extension, but a proposal isn't final and can differ from the final rule.)

If you're unsure whether you qualify, contact ISSS or an ISSS advisor using the details on the [ISSS website](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support).

records.question: Tôi được phép thất nghiệp bao nhiêu ngày?
history: Tôi đang làm OPT sau khi tốt nghiệp.
search_queries: OPT unemployment allowance days
Tôi được phép thất nghiệp bao nhiêu ngày? | Tôi đang làm OPT sau khi tốt nghiệp.
records.answer:
Bạn được phép thất nghiệp **tối đa 90 ngày** trong thời gian OPT sau khi tốt nghiệp (12 tháng đầu).

**Cách tính:**
- Mỗi ngày, kể cả cuối tuần, từ ngày bắt đầu OPT ghi trên thẻ EAD mà bạn không có việc làm đủ điều kiện đều được tính là một ngày thất nghiệp.
- Công việc phải từ **hơn 20 giờ/tuần** để đủ điều kiện (theo định nghĩa của ISSS, toàn thời gian là hơn 20 giờ mỗi tuần). Làm việc từ xa được chấp nhận nếu đáp ứng yêu cầu này.

**Nếu bạn được gia hạn STEM OPT 24 tháng:** bạn có thêm 60 ngày, tổng tối đa là **150 ngày** (90 + 60). Bạn phải báo cho ISSS nếu mất việc hoặc nghỉ việc, và nộp bản đánh giá cuối cùng trên Form I-983 trong vòng 10 ngày.

**Nếu sắp hết giới hạn:** bạn phải hành động **trước ngày thất nghiệp cuối cùng**, ví dụ chuyển sang trường khác, đổi bậc học, rời khỏi Hoa Kỳ, hoặc có biện pháp khác để duy trì tình trạng. Nếu không, bạn sẽ vi phạm tình trạng di trú, và hồ sơ SEVIS có thể bị chấm dứt.

Tình huống của mỗi người khác nhau, nên nếu bạn lo ngại về số ngày thất nghiệp của mình, hãy liên hệ cố vấn ISSS.
